learn.hook: Why would fast young deer need help from a slow old stag? Read on to find out!
points: 'The Old Stag' is a fable. A stag is a male deer.
A fable is a short story where animals talk and act like people. It teaches a lesson called a moral.
Every story has characters (who), a setting (where and when), a problem and a solution.
India has old collections of fables, like the Panchatantra and the Jataka tales.
To find the moral, ask: what did the characters learn at the end?

example.q: Read this fable: In a forest near the Satpura hills lived an old stag named Dhruv. The young deer laughed, "You are so slow, grandpa!" One hot summer, the ponds dried up. The young deer were thirsty and worried. "Follow me," said Dhruv. He walked slowly to a hidden spring behind the big rocks. "I found it many summers ago," he said. The young deer said, "We are sorry. You are slow, but you are wise." Question: What lesson did the young deer learn?
steps: At first, they laughed at Dhruv for being slow.
When there was no water, Dhruv's old memory saved them.
At the end they said, 'You are slow, but you are wise.'
example.answer: Old people may be slow, but they are wise because of their experience. We should respect them.

learn.reallife: Your grandparents know old recipes, games and stories. Ask them. Their experience is a treasure!

games.title: Story order
items: The young deer laughed at slow Dhruv
The ponds dried up in summer
Dhruv led them to a hidden spring

games.title: Parts of the story
pairs: a forest near the Satpura hills

quiz.q: Story line: "In a forest near the Satpura hills lived an old stag named Dhruv." Where did Dhruv live?
options: In a forest near the Satpura hills
quiz.explain: The first line tells us the setting: a forest near the Satpura hills.
quiz.mistake: Does not look for the place words

quiz.q: The young deer laughed, "You are so slow, grandpa!" Why did they laugh at Dhruv?
quiz.explain: They called him 'so slow', so they laughed because he was slow.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a reason not given in the story

quiz.q: Story line: "One hot summer, the ponds dried up." What was the problem in the story?
options: There was no water to drink
quiz.explain: When the ponds dried up, the deer had no water.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand what 'dried up' means

quiz.q: Dhruv said, "I found it many summers ago." How did Dhruv know about the hidden spring?
options: He had found it long ago
He saw it on a map
quiz.explain: 'Many summers ago' means many years ago. He remembered it from long ago.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand 'many summers ago'

quiz.q: What is the moral of the fable about Dhruv?
options: Elders are wise, so we should respect them
Being fast is the only thing that matters
quiz.explain: The young deer learnt that the slow old stag was wise.
quiz.mistake: Picks a detail instead of the lesson

quiz.q: What is a fable?
options: A short story with animals acting like people that teaches a lesson
A news report about real animals
quiz.explain: A fable has animal characters who talk and act like people, and it has a moral.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any animal text is a fable

quiz.q: In "You are slow, but you are wise," what does 'wise' mean?
options: Having good sense from knowing a lot
quiz.explain: A wise person makes good choices because of what they know.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'wise' means fast or strong

quiz.q: The young deer said, "We are sorry." How did they feel at the end?
quiz.explain: They said sorry because they had laughed at Dhruv.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the words the characters say

teach.ask: Gappu laughed at an old crow for flying slowly. Then the old crow showed Gappu where to find water! What can Gappu learn?
teach.praise: Yes! Elders know a lot from experience, so we should respect them and never laugh at them. Gappu has said sorry to the crow!
teach.nudge: What do old animals and people have that young ones may not? How should we treat them?

learn.hook: A stag, a doe and a fawn walk into a forest. Who is who?
points: Wisdom means good sense that comes from learning and experience.
A proverb is a short, wise saying: 'Look before you leap' means think carefully before you act.
'Slow and steady wins the race' means working steadily without giving up brings success.
Male and female names: stag – doe, lion – lioness, peacock – peahen, horse – mare, king – queen.
Young ones: deer – fawn, cat – kitten, dog – puppy, hen – chick, sheep – lamb, lion – cub.

example.q: Think it through: what does 'Look before you leap' mean for Riya, who wants to jump into a puddle?
steps: 'Look before you leap' tells us to check first.
Riya should check how deep or dirty the puddle is before jumping.
example.answer: Think and check carefully before you act.

learn.reallife: Grandparents often use proverbs. Ask yours for a favourite one and what it means!

quiz.q: A stag is a ___ deer.
quiz.explain: A stag is a male deer. A female deer is a doe.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up male and female animal names

quiz.q: What is the female of 'lion'?
quiz.explain: The female of lion is lioness.
quiz.mistake: Picks the female name of a different animal

quiz.q: What is a baby deer called?
quiz.explain: A baby deer is a fawn.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of young animals

quiz.q: What does the proverb 'Look before you leap' mean?
options: Run as fast as you can
quiz.explain: It means we should think before we do something.
quiz.mistake: Takes the words too literally

quiz.q: What does 'Slow and steady wins the race' mean?
options: Working steadily without giving up brings success
quiz.explain: Keeping going steadily, step by step, helps us reach our goal.
quiz.mistake: Takes the proverb to mean the opposite

quiz.q: Which word means the same as 'wise'?
quiz.explain: A wise person is sensible. The others mean the opposite.
quiz.mistake: Picks an antonym instead of a synonym

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'old'?
quiz.explain: 'Young' is the opposite of 'old'. The others mean old.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the same meaning

quiz.q: What is the female of 'peacock'?
quiz.explain: The female of peacock is peahen.
quiz.mistake: Guesses by joining random words

teach.ask: Gappu sees a stag, a doe and a fawn. Can you explain who is who to Gappu?
teach.praise: Correct! The stag is the male deer, the doe is the female deer and the fawn is the baby. Gappu waves at the deer family!
teach.nudge: Which one is the father deer, which is the mother, and which is the baby?

topics.title: Telling the past: past tense verbs

learn.hook: Fables happened 'long, long ago'. So we tell them in the past tense!
points: The past tense tells us about something that has already happened: yesterday, last week, long ago.
Most verbs add -ed: walk → walked, laugh → laughed. If a verb ends in e, add -d: smile → smiled.
Some short verbs double the last letter: stop → stopped, hop → hopped.
If a verb ends in a consonant + y, change y to i and add -ed: cry → cried, dry → dried.
Some verbs change completely: go → went, see → saw, eat → ate, find → found, drink → drank, say → said.

example.q: Think it through: change to the past: 'The old stag finds a spring.'
steps: 'Find' does not take -ed. Its past form is special.
example.answer: The old stag found a spring.

learn.reallife: When you tell your family about your day at school, you use the past tense: I played, I ate, I learnt.

items.text: Yesterday the fawn ___ over a log.
Long ago, Dhruv ___ slowly to the spring.
Last week the young deer ___ at the old stag.

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'go'?
quiz.explain: 'Go' is a special verb. Its past tense is 'went'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to every verb

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'cry'?
quiz.explain: Cry ends in a consonant + y, so y becomes i: cried.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed without changing y to i

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'stop'?
quiz.explain: For 'stop', we double the p and add -ed: stopped.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the last letter

quiz.q: Fill in: "Yesterday, Meena ___ a mango." (eat)
quiz.explain: 'Yesterday' tells us it is the past. The past of eat is ate.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to a special verb

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the past tense?
options: Dhruv will walk to the spring.
Dhruv is walking to the spring.
quiz.explain: 'Walked' tells us the action already happened.
quiz.mistake: Does not look at the verb ending

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'think'?
quiz.explain: 'Think' is a special verb. Its past is 'thought'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to a special verb

quiz.q: Fill in: "Last summer, the young deer ___ sorry to Dhruv." (say)
quiz.explain: The past tense of 'say' is 'said'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ed to 'say'

quiz.q: Which word in "Last week, we visited the zoo" is a verb in the past tense?
quiz.explain: 'Visited' is the action, and -ed shows it is in the past.
quiz.mistake: Picks a time word instead of the verb

teach.ask: Gappu says, 'Yesterday I goed to the river and eated a worm.' Can you help Gappu fix it?
teach.praise: Well done! Yesterday Gappu went to the river and ate a worm. Some past tense verbs are special!
teach.nudge: What is the past of 'go'? And what is the past of 'eat'?
